slots_and_copies.name: eeprom_image
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: single image, no A/B redundancy; validity gated by magic field at 0x04 and a checksum-shaped field at 0x0C whose algorithm is unverified

checksums.name: global_checksum_field
checksums.formula_detail: FUN_0801c224(0,0) compares GetBits(bit=0x40,width=0x20) to XorFoldWords(bit=0x60,range_param=0x73); XorFoldWords (0x080221f0) XORs 32-bit mirror words from the word containing bit_offset through an end word computed as ((range_param*0x800 + UNRESOLVED_CONST) >> 0x10) - start_word + 1. UNRESOLVED_CONST (_DAT_08022224) could not be read from the decompiled text, so the exact covered byte range is unknown.

checksums.name: per_slot_checksum_field
checksums.formula_detail: FUN_0801c224(1,n) compares GetBits(bit=0x80+n*0x140,width=0x20) to XorFoldWords(bit=(0x80+n*0x140)|0x20, range_param=(0x80+n*0x140)+0x140) for n=0..11, i.e. claimed to be the XOR-fold of the 36 data bytes immediately following each slot's 4-byte checksum field. Offset/stride formula confirmed exactly against real .sav; the XOR-fold itself was never exercised in the one available sample (all 12 fields are still the ResetAllSlots() sentinel 0xFFFFFFFF, never recomputed), so the algorithm is unverified.

io_driver_functions.notes: DmaEepromXfer: IME-guarded DMA3-style transfer of a bitstream to/from EEPROM port 0x0D000000, busy-wait on completion. Shared primitive for both EEPROM read and write records.

EepromReadRecord(index,dst8bytes): builds a 2-bit read opcode + 6-bit address bitstream, sends via FUN_0802ee18, clocks 68 bits back, packs 64 data bits into 4x16-bit words at dst. Also called directly 64x from FUN_080220b4 (text-only call edge, not present in callgraph.json).

EepromWriteRecord(index,src8bytes,retry): builds write opcode+address+64 data bits, single DMA burst via FUN_0802ee18, polls EEPROM busy bit with a scanline-count software timeout (wraps at 0xE4=228), returns error code on timeout.
EepromVerifyRecord(index,expected8bytes): calls FUN_0802ee98 to re-read the record, compares all 4 words to expected, returns 0x8000 on mismatch.
EEPROM geometry/backend selector; mode=4 selects the 512-byte/64-record backend actually used (called from FUN_080222c8 before every load).

caller_chains.trigger_context: SaveAll(): untraced caller (game/menu logic) -> for each of 64 records, if dirty-bitmap bit set -> WriteRecordVerified -> EepromWriteRecord -> DMA3 transfer
caller_chains.how_mapped: Traced via grep of ghidra/decompiled.c for literal func_0x... call-site text at lines documented in SAVE-FORMAT-REPORT.md section 3.2; cross-checked caller edge 0x08022078->0x08022268 against ghidra/callgraph.json.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Same WriteRecordVerified call also performs the read-back verify half (EepromVerifyRecord -> EepromReadRecord) before retrying up to 3x on failure.
caller_chains.how_mapped: Text trace of FUN_08022078 body: calls func_0x0802ef48 then func_0x0802f0bc in a 3-iteration retry loop.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Load(): untraced caller -> select EEPROM geometry -> LoadAll() reads all 64 records unconditionally (no verify) into the RAM mirror
caller_chains.how_mapped: Text trace of FUN_080220b4 body (64-iteration loop calling func_0x0802ee98) plus callgraph.json edge 0x080220b4->0x080222c8 caller.

caller_chains.trigger_context: BootCheck(): Load() the EEPROM, then GetBits(0,0x20) magic check against a fixed constant; on mismatch calls ResetAllSlots() which marks every record dirty, rewrites the magic, and invalidates the global + all 12 per-slot checksum fields.
caller_chains.how_mapped: callgraph.json confirms 0x0801cd14 callees include 0x0801c224 and 0x0801ccb8; body text of 0x0801ccb8 shows the SetBits call sequence with the exact bit-offset arithmetic matched against the observed 0x14+n*0x28 pattern in saves/cap-01-future-1.sav.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Independently of the magic check, BootCheck also runs VerifyChecksum(0,0); on failure it applies default settings (0x0801c3e0) rather than a full slot reset.
caller_chains.how_mapped: callgraph.json edge 0x0801cd14->0x0801c224; FUN_0801c224 body text shows the param_1==0 branch bit-offset constants (0x40,0x60,0x73).

fields.name: magic_signature
fields.update_mechanism: SetBits(0,0x20,CONST) inside ResetAllSlots, run when the stored value fails the GetBits(0,0x20)==CONST check at boot
fields.evidence: Code read/write call sites in ghidra/decompiled.c (FUN_0801cd14, FUN_0801ccb8) plus exact byte match in saves/cap-01-future-1.sav; blank in saves/cap-00-future-0.sav

fields.name: global_checksum_or_stat
fields.update_mechanism: SetBits(0x40,0x20,XorFoldWords(0x60,0x73)); algorithm unverified against real byte value (see checksums[0])

observed_values.cap-01-future-1.sav: all zero in all 12 slots (never populated in this sample)

fields.update_mechanism: unknown specific writer in the 187-function trace; coverage range inferred from the checksum-verify arithmetic

fields.name: dirty_bitmap
fields.ram_addr: mirror+0x200 (RAM-only, not part of the 512-byte EEPROM image)
fields.update_mechanism: One bit per 8-byte EEPROM record; SetBits sets the bit for the record containing any field it just changed, iff the underlying word actually changed value
fields.evidence: Direct arithmetic in ghidra/decompiled.c FUN_080220fc/FUN_0802222c/FUN_08022268; not observable in the .sav files since it is RAM-only state

fuzzing_targets.mutation: flip any bit of the "dNoB" magic
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: BootCheck triggers ResetAllSlots: magic restored, all 12 per-slot checksums reset to 0xFFFFFFFF, dirty bitmap forced all-set, full 64-record EEPROM flush on next SaveAll

fuzzing_targets.mutation: set to a value different from the field at offset 8
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Resolves whether 0x0C is a checksum (VerifyChecksum(0,0) fails -> defaults branch) or a mirrored stat (some other system reads 0x08/0x0C as redundant copies) -- the two hypotheses predict different observable branches

fuzzing_targets.mutation: set any per-slot checksum field to a non-0xFFFFFFFF, non-zero value while its 36-byte body stays all-zero
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: VerifyChecksum(1,n) should fail (computed XOR-fold of an all-zero body is 0, not the injected value), excluding the slot from FUN_0801cc40's best-of-N scan; repair by setting the field to 0x00000000 and re-testing for acceptance

fuzzing_targets.mutation: populate a slot body via actual gameplay, then flip one byte
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Requires a fresh capture (not available in this workspace) to first derive the exact XorFoldWords constant, then confirm the game flags/ignores the corrupted slot after repair of the checksum field

open_questions: Exact value of the unresolved global constant feeding XorFoldWords' end-word computation (_DAT_08022224), needed to pin the global checksum's exact covered byte range.

Whether the field at file offset 0x0C is actually a checksum (per FUN_0801c224's read/write call sites) or a mirrored stat duplicate of offset 0x08 (per the observed identical byte value) -- the two hypotheses were not distinguished by the single available non-blank sample.

Identity/semantics of the per-slot 36-byte body (offsets 24, 64, ... within each 40-byte slot) -- plausibly a best-times/leaderboard entry for a racing title, but unproven; no traced writer was found for it.
Identity of bytes 0x00-0x03 (before the magic field) -- never targeted by any traced GetBits/SetBits call.
Exact semantics of FUN_0801c2c0 / FUN_0801c3e0 / FUN_0801c434 settings fields at mirror offsets 0x60-0x73, 0x100, 0x1ae-0x1ba -- traced as writes/defaults but their game meaning is unknown.
The write-verify-retry EEPROM timing behavior (0x0802ef5c's scanline-count timeout) cannot be fuzz-tested from .sav bytes alone; would require emulator-level EEPROM-busy-bit fault injection.

Only one non-blank .sav sample exists in this workspace; a second populated sample (ideally with at least one non-empty leaderboard slot) is required to actually verify the XOR-fold checksum algorithm rather than just its offset arithmetic.
